description: The hand-verified expected result for the DERIVED Joern features fixture. Every value was derived by reading fixtures/derived-joern-features.json and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, and every path was resolved by a second resolver written from the documented indexing scheme alone rather than by importing normalize.paths. The adapter was run only afterwards, to corroborate. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. This fixture is not a capture and does not claim to be one; the captured fixture for this adapter is fixtures/joern.json, with expected/joern.rows.json beside it.
scanner_class_authority: AAP 0.5.4's class table fixes sast for opengrep, semgrep, datadog-static-analyzer and joern. joern is the one of the four that writes a native shape, so it is the only one of them with its own adapter. The value is fixed in advance rather than derived from what the artifact turns out to contain, and it is identical on every row.
artifact_shape_note: This is the only artifact whose shape is the harness's own collector output rather than a tool-native format. There is no Joern output format to look up: harness/bin/run-joern.sh loads the graph with importCpg, runs the bounded query set baked into harness/lib/joern-scan.sc, and that script writes the artifact itself.

fixture.provenance: DERIVED. This document is not an unmodified captured excerpt of any artifact and is not offered as one. Ten of its eleven findings are byte-identical members of harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json's 693 findings and its envelope is that artifact's byte for byte, but the eleventh record was authored, so the file as a whole is a derivation. AAP 0.6.2's captured-positive-mapping requirement is satisfied by fixtures/joern.json instead.
how_it_was_derived: The envelope -- tool, tool_version, cpg, graph, query_set and the whole queries array -- was taken from the raw artifact unchanged, so the shape the adapter reads is the shape the collector writes.
Ten whole findings were taken from the raw artifact unchanged, at raw indexes 10, 14, 15, 16, 95, 238, 371, 656, 669 and 681, in ascending raw order.

One record was authored and inserted at index 7: the org.apache.spark.deploy.master.MasterSuite finding. Its class, its reported line and its query identifier were chosen so that the class resolves uniquely to a real source file in the pinned tree and the line falls inside that file. Nothing is asserted about the call site, and no finding is judged in either direction.
Nothing else was changed: no member was renamed, no value was rewritten and no record was removed.

authored_record.why_it_had_to_be_authored: The raw artifact contains no class whose simple name carries Suite or Test -- measured, 0 of 692 -- because the runbook excludes every -tests JAR from the graph input, so no test-tree class reached the graph the artifact was queried from. The committed dataset holds 107 joern rows and not one with a src/test path.

records_whose_values_are_captured.verification: RawArtifactProvenanceTest in test_joern_adapter.py opens the raw artifact and asserts each of the ten is identical to the raw object under canonical comparison -- json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True) -- and that the authored record is present in the raw artifact under no index at all.

cases_this_fixture_exists_to_exercise: A finding resolving into a src/test tree, RETAINED with in_scope false rather than dropped (AAP 0.5.4 and 0.6.1, and AAP 0.9.3's recorded-not-halting list). This is the case the captured fixture cannot supply, and it is the reason this file exists.
The literal src/test exclusion governing in_scope even though no glob would have matched the path anyway, asserted on a specific row rather than on a count.
A clean parse status: eleven records, eleven rows, no rejection -- the complement of the captured fixture, whose three shaded third-party classes make it partial.
The rows_from_src_test counter reading 1, which is the only place a retained test-tree row is visible: a dropped row and a retained one look identical in a row count.
fixture.why_a_capture_cannot_supply_them: All four rest on a finding whose class resolves into a test tree, and the artifact carries none. Authoring that record into the captured fixture would have made the capture claim false, which is the trade AAP 0.6.2 forbids; dropping the case would have left an AAP requirement with no assertion. Splitting the two is what keeps both claims true.
fixture.re_derivation_trigger: The recorded sha256 above is what makes a later edit to the fixture visible. These rows are re-derived when the fixture changes; the fixture is never edited to suit these rows.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant, which harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py restates as its own FIELDS because AAP 0.6.4 permits an adapter to import paths and severity and nothing else. The two were compared and are identical. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent. path in particular is not an optional field (AAP 0.5.4), so a record whose coordinate cannot be resolved is a counted rejection rather than a row with a null path.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched, or the reason it matched none, is recorded per row under row_derivations.

shape_divergence.summary: The artifact this fixture's envelope and ten of its eleven records come from is written in this provisioning's collector shape, which differs from the collector shape the specification documents. The divergence is recorded, not repaired -- AAP 0.1.3's authority rule -- and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py reads both shapes for exactly that reason, in a fixed field precedence so the choice is reproducible. Three members differ, and each changes a value in the rows below.
shape_divergence.documented_shape: {tool, cpg_path, generated_at, cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size, declaration_index_size, queries: [{id, count}], findings: [{rule_id, message, path, start_line, method_full_name, class_file, path_resolution}]}
shape_divergence.provisioned_shape: {tool, tool_version, cpg, graph: {methods, type_declarations, files}, query_set, queries: [{id, bound, returned, bound_reached, elapsed_ms, callee_prefixes[]}], findings: [{query_id, severity, message, callee, class, method, file, line}]}

differences.documented: findings[].rule_id, one of five joern.-prefixed literals
differences.observed: findings[].query_id, one of the six identifiers harness/lib/joern-scan.sc bakes
differences.consequence: Every rule_id below is a joern- prefixed identifier rather than a joern. prefixed one, read from RULE_ID_FIELDS = ('rule_id', 'query_id') in that precedence, and rule_id_from_query_id counts 11 while rule_id_from_rule_id counts 0.
differences.why_this_is_not_a_guess: The prohibition on taking a rule_id from a queries[].id exists because the documented shape's queries[] carries only {id, count} and records no link between a query and a finding, so any match there would be inference. In this shape each finding carries its own query_id member, so the record itself names the query that produced it and nothing is inferred. KNOWN_RULE_IDS in the adapter carries both vocabularies -- this provisioning's six and the documented five -- and is explicitly never used to filter, because AAP 0.4.2 has the baked query set read from the runner rather than assumed.

differences.documented: no severity member at all, so severity_native null and severity_norm Info on every row
differences.observed: findings[].severity, HIGH or MEDIUM on every record
differences.consequence: Every row below carries severity_native HIGH or MEDIUM and severity_norm High or Medium, with basis label. severity_from_record_label counts 11 and severity_absent counts 0.
differences.why_this_is_the_contract: AAP 0.5.4 places joern under 'No vocabulary at all (gitleaks; joern unless a query defines one)'. Here a query does define one: all six baked queries declare a severity. The no-vocabulary path -- severity_native null with severity_norm Info and the absence stated rather than a level assumed -- is implemented and remains the behaviour for a record carrying no label, and it is simply not the path this artifact takes. Nothing is hard-coded either way: severity.py owns the vocabulary, so this file cannot disagree with severity-map.md.
differences.corroboration: All 107 joern rows in the committed oss-scan-results/findings.json carry severity_native HIGH or MEDIUM. None carries null.

differences.documented: flat cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size and declaration_index_size
differences.observed: a nested graph object carrying methods, type_declarations and files
differences.consequence: envelope_graph_methods, envelope_graph_type_declarations and envelope_graph_files carry the graph's figures, while envelope_collector_source_index_size and envelope_collector_declaration_index_size stay 0 because the flat members are absent. The per-query tally is spelled returned here rather than count, and neither is summed into any published figure.

shape_divergence.path_resolution_member: Absent from this fixture entirely: this provisioning's collector emits no path_resolution, so collector_explanation_present is 0. The rule it is subject to is unchanged and is structural rather than conditional -- AAP 0.5.4 has any collector explanation for an unmappable bytecode path retained in the rejection record and in no dataset field, and a twelve-key row has nowhere to put one. The same holds for the documented findings[].path member, which this fixture also does not carry, so collector_path_refused, collector_path_corroborated and collector_path_disagreed are all 0.
shape_divergence.file_member: Every record carries a file member holding the frontend's ephemeral extraction path. It is never read as a path. harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json names it record_path_field_to_ignore for exactly this reason, and the class member -- named record_path_field -- is the only resolvable coordinate.

count_unit.per_query_tally_member: queries[].returned in this shape; queries[].count in the documented shape
count_unit.which_one_is_the_raw_count: len(findings) = 11. The sum of the per-query tallies is 692 and is not the raw count and is not published as one.
count_unit.why_they_differ: The fixture carries 11 findings while carrying the raw artifact's queries[] array unchanged, and that array's tallies sum to the whole 692-finding artifact. The two numbers therefore differ by construction, which is what makes the reconciliation assertion non-vacuous: an implementation that counted the per-query tallies instead of the findings would produce 692 against 11 rows and fail rather than silently agree.
count_unit.authority: AAP 0.5.4 makes findings[] the reconciliation unit, and normalize.reconcile.count_records walks that same unit without building rows. The adapter deliberately publishes no count of the findings it walked, so that the left-hand side of the identity cannot be taken from the traversal that builds the right-hand side.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of findings[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.note: Every one of the eleven classes resolves to exactly one distinct source path in the pinned tree, so every record becomes a row and this derived fixture produces no rejection -- which is deliberate: it is the clean-parse complement of the captured fixture, whose three shaded third-party classes make it partial. The unresolvable and ambiguous cases are covered by fixtures/joern.json, reject-joern-unresolvable-path.json and reject-joern-ambiguous-path.json.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): 43 keys -- 23 authored, 5 envelope integers, one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member, one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member, and one provenance key per member of each field-candidate tuple. The keys above are in COUNTER_KEYS order and the set is complete: every key the adapter initialises appears, so a zero here means measured-zero rather than not-measured.
counters_note: Three groups deserve reading together. The row decomposition rows_in_scope 8 + rows_out_of_scope 3 sums to the row count, because it is one measurement split rather than a second count of the same thing. The six source_index_* keys describe the index the resolution ran against rather than the records, and they are the figures that make a rejection count interpretable -- source_index_supplied 0 records that the adapter built the index over the pinned root rather than being handed one, so a test injecting a synthetic index through SourceIndex.from_mapping changes exactly these keys and nothing else. The five envelope_* graph keys are metadata for tool-status.md and contribute nothing to any record count.

aap_reported_counters.note: AAP 0.5.4 has four counters reported per tool. Two are members of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS and two are not, and the reason the two are absent is structural rather than an omission.

multi_location_records.basis: No finding in this shape carries a locations array; each names exactly one call site through its class, method and line members. The counter is published anyway, so that a future collector emitting several locations is visible rather than silently reduced to its first.

non_filesystem_paths.basis: Every path below has kind bytecode_source, which normalize.paths.is_non_filesystem_kind excludes -- only outside_root and archive_member are non-filesystem coordinates. Each resolved path names a real file in the pinned tree.

multi_valued_cwe_records.basis: Not a member of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS; the SARIF adapter publishes it because a SARIF rule can carry several CWE tokens. A Joern finding names a bytecode call site rather than a weakness catalogue entry, so cwe is null on every row by contract and the count is structurally 0. Manufacturing a CWE from a class name or a query identifier would be inference.

multi_valued_cve_records.basis: Not a member of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS, for the same reason: this shape carries no advisory identifier, so cve is null on every row by contract and the count is structurally 0.

envelope_fields.note: The envelope members outside findings[] are not findings and produce no rows. They must not appear in any row, and a twelve-key row makes that structural. They are recorded here because build-record.md and run-record.md cross-reference the graph figures, and a number that reaches no channel reaches no document.

documented_members_absent.cpg_methods: absent -- the figure arrives as graph.methods instead, and the counter envelope_graph_methods carries it
documented_members_absent.cpg_typedecls: absent -- the figure arrives as graph.type_declarations instead, and the counter envelope_graph_type_declarations carries it

envelope_fields.cpg_member: The envelope also carries a cpg member naming the graph file. It is an absolute path in the artifact and is deliberately not copied into this file, which stays free of absolute paths; the graph's identity is recorded in run-record.md by byte size and sha256.
envelope_fields.bound_reached: No query reports reaching its traversal bound, so no per-query result below is truncated. Truncation is read from the flag rather than assumed, because a truncated query's silence would otherwise be indistinguishable from a clean one.

resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the joern entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.why_no_filesystem_base_exists: The runner queries a graph the frontend built over staged JARs rather than over the source tree, so the emitted file member is by construction the frontend's extraction path for a .class member and can never be a path in the Spark tree. The metadata therefore records a null base value rather than inventing a plausible one, and the class member is the only resolvable coordinate.
resolution_context.resolution_procedure: The class member -- a dotted type full name -- is reduced by normalize.paths.class_key to <package path>/<outer type name>, truncating the basename at its first $ so a companion object, an anonymous class and a nested class all collapse to the outer type. That key is then looked up in a source index over src/main and src/test under the pinned root, across two key schemes: by_filename on <package dir>/<file base name>, and by_decl on <package dir>/<declared type name>. The union of candidates must be exactly one distinct path.
resolution_context.gap_1_closed: The index spans src/main and src/test rather than src/main alone. Every -tests artifact the build emitted is in the graph input, so a finding can legitimately name bytecode compiled from a test tree, and row 7 is that case.
resolution_context.gap_2_closed: A resolution is taken only where the union of candidates is exactly one distinct path. Two or more is ambiguous_source_resolution with every competing candidate named, never a first-wins pick. Closing gap 1 increases ambiguity, which is why closing gap 2 is mandatory rather than optional.
resolution_context.declaration_scheme_is_not_optional: Two of the eleven rows resolve on the declaration scheme alone -- ProcessBuilderLike is declared in DriverRunner.scala and ObjectInputStreamWithLoader in Checkpoint.scala. A filename-only index would lose both silently, and a silently lost row is indistinguishable from a class with nothing to report.
resolution_context.root_dependence: Unlike the SARIF fixtures, these rows depend on a live tree: the class-to-source resolution reads the pinned checkout at $SPARK_SRC. Every emitted path is expressed relative to that root and none is absolute. The index figures under counters are the measurement over the pinned tree, and they reproduce the figures the adapter's own docstring records.
resolution_context.severity_source: Every record states its own severity label, so severity_native is that literal verbatim and severity_norm comes from severity.py's label table: HIGH High, MEDIUM Medium. The label governs whenever it is in the mapped vocabulary and no score is consulted, which is the label-over-score precedence severity-map.md states.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A Joern finding names a bytecode call site rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry. The absence is explicitly not a rejection: the unformable_package_coordinate class covers a dependency-oriented record, and this shape is not one.

independent_resolver.method: Every path below was first resolved by a second resolver written from the documented indexing scheme alone, which does not import normalize.paths. It reproduced the adapter's own recorded index measurements exactly: 6759 files indexed, 6755 by_filename keys of which 4 are ambiguous, and 15230 by_decl keys of which 107 are ambiguous.

adapter_run.when: after the hand derivation, never before it
adapter_run.note: Running the adapter over the fixture with the recorded runner metadata and the pinned root reproduces all twelve fields of all eleven rows and all 43 counter values. That is corroboration recorded after the fact, not the source of these values.

committed_dataset.note: The ten records whose values are captured appear in the committed dataset with every one of the twelve fields in agreement. The eleventh, the authored MasterSuite record, is absent from the dataset exactly as its provenance predicts -- the raw artifact carries no test-tree class -- and the dataset holds no joern row with a src/test path at all. Its absence there is therefore consistent evidence rather than a discrepancy.

row_derivations_note: One entry per row, in row order. Each names the fixture member every field was read from, the class key the coordinate reduced to, which index scheme resolved it, and either the allowlist glob the path matched or the reason it matched none. file_line_count_at_the_pin is the resolved file's real length in the pinned checkout, which is what makes each start_line checkable rather than merely plausible.

row_derivations.scope_reason: out of scope: the path matches none of the twelve allowlist globs. launcher is not among the scope roots, so a legitimately resolved finding in it is kept with in_scope false and counted rather than dropped.
in scope: matched the allowlist glob core/src/main/**
in scope: matched the allowlist glob core/src/main/**

row_derivations.class_key_note: The basename is truncated at its first $, so the anonymous class ProcessBuilderLike$$anon$3 collapses to the outer type ProcessBuilderLike -- the same reduction the collector performs, which is what lets a key built here match one built there.
row_derivations.declaration_evidence: No file is named ProcessBuilderLike.scala, so the filename scheme finds nothing and only the declaration scheme resolves this key. In the pinned tree core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/deploy/worker/DriverRunner.scala declares trait ProcessBuilderLike at line 269 and object ProcessBuilderLike at line 274, with the anonymous instance at lines 275-277. Line 276 of that file is the override of start() that calls processBuilder.start(), which is the callee this record names.
row_derivations.scope_reason: in scope: matched the allowlist glob core/src/main/**

row_derivations.class_key_note: The trailing $ marks the companion object and is removed by the same first-$ truncation.
row_derivations.scope_reason: in scope: matched the allowlist glob sql/connect/**/src/main/**, which requires the mid-path ** to match the single directory segment common
in scope: matched the allowlist glob common/network-yarn/src/main/**

row_derivations.declaration_evidence: No file is named ObjectInputStreamWithLoader.scala; the type is declared inside streaming/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/streaming/Checkpoint.scala, so only the declaration scheme resolves it. This is the second of the two rows a filename-only index would lose silently.
row_derivations.scope_reason: out of scope: the path matches none of the twelve allowlist globs. streaming is not among the scope roots, so this legitimately resolved finding is kept with in_scope false and counted.

row_derivations.purpose: This is the row this expected file exists for. AAP 0.5.4 requires that a finding resolving into src/test be retained with in_scope false rather than dropped, and AAP 0.9.3 repeats it among the recorded-not-halting conditions. A dropped test-tree row and a retained one look identical in a row count, so the assertion has to be made on a specific row.
row_derivations.candidates_note: Exactly one source file in either tree claims this key, so the resolution is unique and the record is a row rather than an ambiguous_source_resolution rejection. That is worth stating because a neighbouring key is not unique: org/apache/spark/SparkContextSuite is claimed by both core and hadoop-cloud, and a key like that is rejected rather than resolved to whichever file the index saw first.
row_derivations.scope_reason: out of scope: the path contains the literal src/test. No glob matches core/src/test/... in any case, and the literal exclusion would override a positive glob match if one existed -- normalize.paths.in_scope applies that rule before consulting the globs. The row is retained and counted under rows_from_src_test.
row_derivations.what_is_asserted: That this class resolves uniquely to this source path, that 218 is inside the file's 252 lines, and that the row is retained with in_scope false. Nothing is asserted about the call site: the record is derived, and no finding is judged in either direction.

row_derivations.class_key_note: An org.apache.hive package rather than org.apache.spark, vendored into the Thrift server module. The resolution is by package path and type name and is indifferent to the top-level namespace.
row_derivations.scope_reason: in scope: matched the allowlist glob sql/hive-thriftserver/src/main/**
in scope: matched the allowlist glob sql/catalyst/src/main/**
in scope: matched the allowlist glob sql/catalyst/src/main/**

fields_absent_on_every_row.cwe: A Joern finding names a bytecode call site, not a weakness catalogue entry, and this shape carries no CWE member. Deriving one from a query identifier would be inference.
fields_absent_on_every_row.cve: The same: this shape carries no advisory identifier.
fields_absent_on_every_row.package_coordinate: The same, and the absence is explicitly not a rejection condition here -- unformable_package_coordinate covers a dependency-oriented record, which this is not.

members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.note: Each of these is present in the fixture and must not appear in any row. Checked by substring comparison against every field of every row above, not merely by inspection.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.method: The enclosing method's full signature. Carried into a rejection's identity as diagnosable context, never into a row -- and never into message, however readable it looks.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.file: The frontend's ephemeral extraction path for a .class member. The runner metadata names it record_path_field_to_ignore, and it is never read as a path; reading it as one would relativize a temporary directory into a plausible-looking wrong answer for every row.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.path_resolution: Not present in this fixture at all. Were it present, AAP 0.5.4 confines it to the rejection record and to no dataset field, so it would still reach no row.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.envelope_members: tool_version, cpg, graph, query_set and queries are envelope metadata: not findings, and they produce no rows.
